fixed.explanation: TryPushdownPrefixFilter only recognized functions named "prefix". The starts_with function (and the ^@ operator) is bound under the name "starts_with", so it was never converted into range filters (s >= prefix AND s < next_prefix) and row groups weren't pruned. Accepting both names enables the pushdown.

query.intent: Optimizer rule that rewrites LIKE 'prefix%' into range comparisons (s >= 'prefix' AND s < 'prefix+1') for filter pushdown and row group pruning should also handle starts_with(s, 'prefix') and the prefix operator ^@, which are currently left as opaque filters.
query.symptom: starts_with(s, 'x') and s ^@ 'x' filters are not converted into range filters so zone-map pruning scans all row groups, unlike LIKE 'x%'.

history.analysis: FilterCombiner::TryPushdownPrefixFilter handles prefix and starts_with pushdown, and TryPushdownLikeFilter handles LIKE. LIKE becomes a range filter and prunes row groups. starts_with and ^@ are still left as opaque filters, so the pushdown in TryPushdownPrefixFilter probably doesn't produce a range filter or doesn't apply in this case. I only saw truncated snippets of these functions, so this is a moderate-confidence guess.
